paper_title: Gated Attention for Large Language Models Non-linearity, Sparsity, and   Attention-Sink-Free
caption_used: Massive activation values across layers under baseline conditions, showing four component signals. The ffn_residual (red solid) and attn_residual (orange dotted) lines rise sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400, with ffn_residual maintaining values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20 before declining. The attn_residual closely mirrors ffn_residual but with a one-layer rightward shift. The ffn_output (green dash-dot) exhibits periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, reaching peak values of approximately 800. The attn_output (blue dashed) remains near zero throughout all layers, with no notable increase at any point in the network. The data indicates that massive activations in the baseline are driven primarily by the feed-forward network residual stream, with attention outputs contributing negligibly.

model_annotations.Bulgarian:
The line graph illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers under baseline conditions for four component signals. The X-axis is labeled "Layer" and ranges from 0 to 22 with uniform intervals of 5 units. The Y-axis is labeled "Max Activation Value" and spans from 0 to 1600, also with uniform intervals of 200 units. Both axes have a linear scale.

The graph displays four distinct lines, each representing a different component signal: attn_output (blue dashed line), attn_residual (orange dotted line), ffn_output (green dash-dot line), and ffn_residual (red solid line). The attn_output line remains relatively stable near zero throughout all layers, with no significant fluctuations. The attn_residual line exhibits a sharp increase at layer 5, reaching approximately 1400, and then continues to rise slightly before declining after layer 20. The ffn_residual line also shows a steep rise at layer 5, reaching around 1400, and maintains values between 1400 and 1600 through layer 20 before decreasing. The ffn_output line displays periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, peaking at approximately 1400, 500, and 1200 respectively. Overall, the graph highlights the varying patterns of maximum activation values across different layers for the four component signals.

model_annotations.English: The plot illustrates the maximum activation values across different layers for four component signals under baseline conditions. The x-axis represents the layer number, ranging from 0 to 22 with a linear scale and integer tick labels at intervals of 5. The y-axis represents the maximum activation value, ranging from 0 to 1600 with a linear scale and tick labels at intervals of 200. The plot displays four lines: "attn_output" (blue dashed line), which remains near zero throughout all layers, starting at approximately 20 at layer 0 and ending at around 1240 at layer 22; "attn_residual" (orange dotted line), which rises sharply at layer 5 to approximately 1400, continues to rise to around 1500 by layer 7, and remains between 1500 and 1550 until layer 20 before declining to around 600 at layer 22; "ffn_output" (green dash-dot line), which exhibits periodic spikes at layers 5, 13, and 22, reaching peak values of approximately 1400, 500, and 800 respectively, with values near zero at other layers; and "ffn_residual" (red solid line), which also rises sharply at layer 5 to around 1450, maintains values between 1450 and 1550 through layer 20, and then declines to approximately 440 at layer 22.
